prompt: Use case: identity-preserve narrative restaging. First inputs canonical identity portraits; next room master is only architectural/palette reference; LAST input is prior scene for cast, approved face morphology and exact task content, NOT a pose to preserve. Preserve each canonical face, adult age, hair, eye/nose/jaw proportions and characteristic accessories. Farah lens anatomical LEFT eye; Demir comms anatomical RIGHT ear; Nazari and Mirza have no eyewear. Balanced stylized adult head/body scale, neither oversized heads nor realistic tiny heads. Clean cel-shaded adventure-comic linework, natural supported anatomy, two arms per character. Completely RESTAGE as a candid bridge review between Farah and Commander Mirza. Farah sits at a sloping console, torso and head naturally angled toward the replay record. Mirza leans over the opposite corner with one hand on the rail and the other pointing at the later-period column, lips pursed and one eyebrow raised in an insistent question. Farah looks up toward Mirza with a thoughtful, serious expression, stylus resting on the relevant row and her free hand near the console. Camera is at their side, catching both three-quarter faces and the shared work surface. No one looks at viewer, no held-up card or tablet, no paired portrait. The single compact work screen shows Earlier period and Later period as two columns under One-step replay, with Observed history under both and the note Predictions not fed to later inputs. No invented MAE or success values. The figures are assessing the comparison method; keep their questioning gestures and shared attention dominant. All rear displays and unused holo emitter off. Preserve the bridge room architecture, warm lamp light, muted sage and brass, natural skin, no neon. Output one full 1536x1024 scene. No text outside genuine work artifacts, no captions, no hero portraits, no camera-facing eye contact or lesson cards.

iterations.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit with immutable canonical identity. Cinematic Deep Orbit adventure-comic scene,1536x1024. First reference images are canonical faces, next is bridge master for room/palette, LAST is exact scene to edit. Preserve exact people, facial morphology, adult age markers, warm skin, nose/jaw/eye proportions, hair, side-specific accessories, expressions, story action and entire room composition. Keep every continuous shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand chain, grips, torso/head alignment, thighs, chair support and rail contacts intact. Demir comms anatomical RIGHT ear, Farah lens anatomical LEFT eye. Make only requested screens and small proportional adjustments. Keep narrative people dominant; embed concise task meaning in existing screens rather than turning scene into a full technical infographic. All peripheral monitors, wrist displays and unmentioned readable displays must be OFF, plain charcoal glass with no arbitrary bars, waveforms, gauges or text. Retain physical buttons. Muted sage, aged brass and charcoal with natural warm skin; no neon mint, cyan or mustard wash. Preserve Farah pointing at tablet and holding its edge with other hand, Mirza full stance andrailcontact, both exact faces and expressions. Both heads can be adjusted only slightly, around95 percent current size, with natural necks, samefaceproportions. Tablet replaces arbitrary waveforms with a concise comparison headed "Compare errors". Two side-by-side cards: "Earlier period" with "1-step replay" and "Later period" with "1-step replay". Below both, one shared note "Observed history". No invented numeric errors or verdict. One background monitor directly between their heads may carry the short lesson reminder "Predictions can feed later inputs"; do not add graphs. Other screens OFF. Do not imply errors always rise or that error growth proves drift. cel-shaded cartoon illustration, clean bold linework, flat shading with one soft key light, slightly stylized proportions, cinematic character and environment framing, near-black space beyond the viewports, green #6BAA8A interface glow and rim light, warm brass #A89060 metal trim, cohesive series look, not photorealistic. Output one full scene only.
